answer: Rule: every identity stores one unique orchard shard of network data and proves it on demand. The shard is assigned by lottery, so a yarrow cannot fake a second copy: proof-of-replication catches duplicates and burns a 60-unit bond. One fake costs 60 units plus real disk and bandwidth; ten fakes cost 600 units plus ten shards to serve. The audit signal arrives at random times, and a missed proof slashes the bond the same epoch. Storage cannot be shared, so cost scales linearly with every fake.
